paragraphs.text: This lesson is about the two things you talk about most in a new country: how your day runs, and who your family is. You will learn to understand and say the time, to make a time statement, to talk about your family, to make an arrangement, to arrange an appointment on the phone, and to excuse yourself when you are late.

Meet Kaan. His day is the spine of the first pages. Read his sentences and notice how little grammar is doing the work — the words in the middle tell you when, and the verb tells you what happens. Look at the example in the speech bubble: {{de:Am Morgen duscht Kaan. Dann frühstückt er und liest …}}
Am Morgen duscht Kaan. Dann frühstückt er und liest Nachrichten. Am Sonntag schläft er lange.

First you will match Kaan's photos to sentences like {{de:Kaan geht in die Mensa}} and {{de:Er besucht seine Oma}}, then you will hear the same story and number the pictures. Listen for the time words first — they are your order of events.

items.german: Dann frühstückt er und liest Nachrichten.
items.english: Then he has breakfast and reads the news.

items.german: Am Abend besucht er seine Oma.
items.english: In the evening he visits his grandma.

items.german: mit der Familie zu Mittag essen
